rogue.summary: The mantle is now skinned. The cap over each shoulder follows the upper arm, and the collar and the front and back panels stay on the chest. In attack2 and victory, the upper arms stay under the mantle. The dagger blades are now about 30 percent longer and 15 percent wider, with the same grip. The forge check shows result ok and ground ok, with a head margin of 0.3 cm.
strengths: In attack2, a raised arm lifts the mantle cap like a pauldron. The arm stays under the cloth, and the mantle does not tear.
The longer blades read as silver lines in the attack2 and victory sprites. The crossed daggers in the victory pose are clear from the front.
The hood, the face, the gold clasp, and the hem stitches still match the mockup, and all 8 clips are present.
issues: In attack2 at t = 0.32 s, the mantle cap over the raised arm still ends in a pointed flap. It looks like a small wing for about 0.2 s.

The top of the left bracer shows through the side of the mantle, also in the rest pose. In victory, the daggers go 0.9 cm into the mantle, and in the attack, the left dagger goes 0.6 cm into the sheath.
At 128 px the blades are still thin, and the old shape issues remain: the hood is very deep from the side, and the tunic is short and plain.
next: Round the mantle hem over the shoulders, so the lifted cap has no corner. Move the bracer in, or the mantle out, so the bracer stays under the cloth.
Move the victory cross pose 1 cm forward, and move the attack slash 1 cm away from the sheaths.

archer.summary: The archer matches the mockup well and now has the full hero clip set. The bow shot draws the string and releases a nocked arrow. The bow is still small and dark.
strengths: The attack draws the string back with a nocked arrow and then releases it. The shot reads clearly in the side view.
In the death clip, the archer staggers, falls on the back, and lies still. The bow drops to the floor next to the body.
The hood point, the elf ears, and the quiver with gold fletching give a clear silhouette in all 8 sprite directions.
issues: In the front view, the bow passes in front of the face while it rises and falls. The check shows a head margin of only 0.3 cm.
The bow and the lower string go 1.0 to 1.9 cm into the tunic and the belt in attack and attack2. The arrow is thin and dark and reads weakly.
The bow is still smaller and darker than the large recurve in the mockup. The hood rim is still thick, and the legs still look short.
next: Make the bow 20 percent larger and use a lighter wood color. This item from the last review is still open.
Move the bow path away from the face and the tunic in attack and attack2. The thinner hood rim from the last review is also still open.

knight.summary: The knight is very close to the mockup and now has the full hero clip set. The helmet, the red plume, the heart shield, and the red cape read clearly at 128 px.
strengths: Steel, gold, and red cloth read as clearly different materials in the model and in the sprites.
The clip set is complete: idle, walk, run, a sword slash, a shield bash, hit, death, and victory. The feet stay planted in the walk and the run.
The shield stays clear of the face at rest, and no held item passes through the head in any clip.
issues: In the victory clip, the raised sword reaches only the brow of the helmet. In the slash, the body hides the sword during the wind-up.
The rig has no knees. The legs stay stiff when he falls and lies on the ground in the death clip.

Small contacts remain: the left gauntlet goes up to 1.1 cm into the cuirass in the death and the shield bash. The helmet has ear discs only, not the cheek guards of the mockup. At 65,322 triangles, the knight is the heaviest model.
next: Add small cheek guards to the helmet.
Move the mail ring pattern into the normal map if the triangle count must go down.

wizard.summary: The wizard is a fire mage with a large red hat, a forked fire staff, and a flame in her left palm. The front matches the mockup well. The back and the staff are simpler than in the mockup. All 8 clips work. The death clip now ends with her flat on her back.
strengths: The hat has a soft wavy brim, a curled tip, a brown band, and a gold flame badge. It gives her a clear silhouette in all 8 sprite directions.
The front has the gold V trim, the belt with the red gem, the flame motifs on the coat, and the cape that flares out on both sides.
In the death clip, she staggers, falls back, and lies flat. The legs lie in line with the body, the coat follows the legs, the cape lies flat under her, and both flames go out.
issues: The back of the cape is one plain red area with only a gold hem. From the back and the side, the hat and the cape merge into one red mass, also at sprite size.
The staff is a thin straight pole with a small fork. In the mockup, the staff is a thick twisted branch that holds the orb. The palm flame is also smaller than in the mockup.

At the end of the death clip, the hat stands upright on her face, and the bare skin at the top of the head shows from the side. In the walk, the long coat hides the legs, so the stride is weak from the side.
next: Add a gold flame emblem and a trim band to the back of the cape, and make the cape a darker red than the hat.
Make the staff a thicker twisted branch with a fork that wraps around the orb, and make the palm flame larger.

cleric.summary: The cleric is a dwarf battle priest with a ginger mane, a braided beard, a large cross hammer, and a holy book. The front silhouette matches the mockup, and all eight clips are done: idle, walk, run, attack, attack2, hit, death, and victory.
strengths: The front silhouette matches the mockup: the large octagonal hammer on the right, the big ginger head, and the book with gold corners on the left.
The attack is a clear overhead smash. The hammer rises behind the head, goes over the top, and hits the ground in front of the dwarf.
The death has a stagger back, a fall, and a rest on the back. The hammer and the book stay in the hands and lie on the ground.
issues: The brows point down at the center and the eyes are large and round, so the face looks stern and young. The mockup face is older and smiles.
The side braids and their rings are short and small, so they do not show in the front view. The hair and the beard are smooth, with few strand grooves.

In the attack, the right bracer goes 0.9 cm into the collar while the hammer is up. The model has 85,000 triangles, which is the highest count of the heroes. In the east and west sprites, the hair covers most of the face.
next: Raise the brows, make the eyes a little smaller, and add heavier lower lids, for an older and friendlier face.
Make the two side braids longer, with larger gold rings, and cut deeper strand grooves in the hair and the beard.

druid.summary: The druid reads as the mushroom girl at once, and all 8 clips pass the check. The staff, the apron, and the belt still differ from the mockup. At 72,196 triangles, she is the heaviest model in the set.
strengths: The large spotted cap with the cream rim and the gills gives a unique silhouette in every view and in all 8 sprites.
The face is very close to the mockup: large brown eyes, pink cheeks, a small smile, and a ginger bob.
The clip set is complete: idle, walk, run, a staff cast, a flask throw, hit, death, and victory. The cap and the lantern lag and overshoot in the hit and the victory.
issues: The staff is still thin and straight, and the lantern is small. The mockup staff is thick and gnarled, with a large lantern on a hook.
The front is plain. The apron is a flat card with one clover, and the three belt pouches and the small hip potion are too small to read.

The attacks read weakly. The staff cast is a flat thrust at hip height with no spell effect, and the thrown flask is small with no splash. At the end of the death clip, the cap stands on its rim and hides the body in the side view.
next: Make the staff thicker and gnarled, and hang a larger lantern from a hook at the top.
Make the three belt pouches and the hip potion larger, and give the apron a scalloped hem with the mushroom motif.

adventurer.summary: The adventurer is a chibi hero with a teal bandana, a red scarf, a leather harness, a short sword, a map, and a large pack with a bedroll and a lantern. It matches the mockup in the face, the clothes, the pack, and the lantern. The hair, the bedroll, and the hand that holds the map differ from the mockup. All 8 clips pass the forge check.
strengths: The face reads at 128 px in the sprites: large brown eyes with highlights, rosy cheeks, and an open smile. The red scarf, the cream shirt, the harness, and the belt match the mockup.
The pack reads from all 8 sprite directions: the teal bedroll, the brass lantern on the side, and the flap with a buckle. The silhouette is clear in every view.

The full clip set is present: idle, walk, run, attack, attack2, hit, death, and victory. The death staggers, pitches forward, and ends face down under the pack. The forge check shows result ok and ground ok.
issues: The front hair stands up in a spiky crown, but the mockup hair sweeps to one side. At the back and the sides, the hair is one smooth mass, like a helmet.
In the attack wind-up (t = 0.2 to 0.3 s), the head and the pack hide the sword in the three-quarter and side views. The blade passes only 0.3 cm from the head.
The legs stay straight in every clip. The death fall tips the body forward as one rigid piece, and the attack2 lunge has no knee bend.
next: Add knee bones, so the run, the attack2 lunge, and the death fall bend the legs.
Sculpt the front hair to sweep to one side as in the mockup, and add separate locks to the back and the sides of the head.

goblin-warrior.summary: The goblin warrior stays close to the four-view mockup in every view. The hair on the crown is now one soft crest that leans back, as in the mockup. Each ear now has a slight cup and rolls 28 degrees, so its inner face looks a little upward. In the SW and SE sprites, the far ear still shows as a narrow upward point. The forge check shows result ok and ground ok.
strengths: The one soft crest replaces the three thin spikes. From the front it is a round, soft shape. From the side it leans back like a small flame.
The broad leaf ears, the angry eyes, and the fang read at once. The face reads at 128 px in the S, SW, and SE sprites.
All identity cues of the mockup are present: the nicked ear, one shoulder guard, the diagonal strap, the pouch, the wraps, and the dagger. At 30,374 triangles, the model is light.
issues: In the SW and SE sprites, the far ear still reads as a narrow point above the head. The raised camera looks along the ear, and the head hides the wide base of the ear.
The belt buckle is still smaller than the large tan buckle in the mockup.
The pouch is at the front of the hip, so it does not show from the back as in the mockup. The brows are thicker than the thin brows of the mockup.
next: Turn the ears more to the front (about 20 degrees of sweep instead of 32), or let the tips droop a little. Then compare the front silhouette with the mockup again.
Make the belt buckle about 30 percent larger.

horned-boar.summary: The horned boar is a strong chibi monster. The hoof soles are now solid black, and the attack is a real gore: a low gather, a 0.2 m charge, and a hooked toss. The short snout in profile is the largest open fault.
strengths: The attack has clear stages. The head drops until the snout is at knee height, and the horns and the tusks point forward. The hips then drive 0.2 m forward, and the head hooks up and to the left.
The legs in the attack use two-bone IK. The hind hooves stay planted and roll onto the toe as the legs push. The front hooves step forward and back, and no hoof slides or goes into the floor.
The shin fur now ends inside the hooves, at y = 0.023. In the death, the raised soles show solid black discs, with no brown ring.
issues: The snout is still short in profile. In the side view and in the W and E sprites, the snout is only a small pink edge, and the head looks flat.
When the head is low in the attack, the lower jaw goes into the front of the chest. From the side, the head and the chest merge into one mass.
Each hoof cleft cuts through the full hoof height. On a raised sole, a thin brown line of shin fur shows inside the cleft.
next: Make the snout 20 percent longer. A longer snout gives a boar profile in the side view, the W and E sprites, and the attack.
Stop the hoof cleft below the hoof top, or fill the hoof inside it with black, so no fur shows in the cleft.

goblin-archer.summary: The goblin archer has its full clip set: idle, walk, run, a bow shot, hit, and death. The shot is now a real bow shot. The goblin nocks an arrow, pulls the string back to the chin, holds, and releases. The hood, the ears, the face, and the leather gear match the mockup.
strengths: The pointed dark hood with the ears through it gives a strong, unique silhouette in every view and in every sprite direction.
The shot reads. The string bends back to the right fist, a nocked arrow shows from the nock to the release, and the string snaps straight when the arrow goes.
The bow cants its top out to the right, so the upper limb stays beside the face. Both eyes stay clear in the front and three-quarter views at full draw.
issues: The short arms and the big hood keep the draw short and low. The right fist anchors under the chin, not at the jaw. In the side view, the hood and the body hide the right fist.
The ears are thin flat plates. In the side views and in the W and E sprites, they read as flat triangles. In the SW and SE sprites, they read as thin sticks.
The model differs from the mockup. It has no long back cape and no chest strap, and the nose is a small bump, not a snout. In the draw, the lower string touches the capelet by 0.9 cm.
next: Give the ears thickness and a cupped inner face, as in the mockup. Then the ears read as ears from the side and from above.
Add the long back cape and the chest strap from the mockup, and keep the lower bowstring clear of the capelet in the draw.

skeleton.summary: The skeleton warrior matches the enemy-sheet design: a grinning skull with glowing eyes under a riveted helmet, a red scarf, mail, a sword, and a round red shield. It now has the full clip set: idle, walk, run, attack, hit, and death. The forge check shows result ok and ground ok. The helmet is still dark iron, and the chop stops at the impact.
strengths: The death clip tells a clear story. The skeleton staggers, its knees buckle, and it folds into a heap. Then the helmeted skull rolls off beside the body, and the sword and the shield fall flat.
In the chop, the flat of the blade faces sideways, so the edge leads down through the cut. The wind-up now goes up and back over the right shoulder.
The slanted black sockets, the amber eyes, and the square teeth make a clear angry skull face. Iron, mail, bone, red cloth, wood, and brass read as different materials.
issues: The chop is a real sword cut only in part. The edge leads, but the huge helmet hides the raised blade in the three-quarter and side views, and the tip stays below the helmet crown. The blade stops at waist height and holds, so there is no follow-through.

The helmet is still dark iron all over. The mockup shows lighter steel with dark patches. From above, the dark dome is the largest shape in the sprites, and the face shows only in the three front directions.
The model stands in a neutral pose, but the mockup shows a lunge. The mockup has brown leather boots; the model has plain steel feet. The sword passes 0.3 cm from the head in the check.
next: Make the helmet steel lighter, with the patina in patches. This item from the old review is still open.
Lift the sword tip above the helmet crown in the wind-up, and continue the cut down past the waist before the recovery. The old item for a higher wind-up is open in part.

orc-warrior.summary: The orc warrior is a stocky brute with a heavy scowl, tusks, a topknot, a spiked pauldron, and a large crescent axe. The one-hand overhead chop now hits at the height of a target's body in front of the orc. The follow-through goes down and across the body and stops above the floor. The clip check passes the head test and the ground test.
strengths: The attack reads as a hit on a body: the axe comes over the top, hits level in front of the chest with the edge down, and follows through across the body to the left knee.
The costume matches the mockup: large brown bracers, a spiked pauldron, a belt with a round buckle, a ragged red loincloth, and fur leg wraps.
The death reads well at game size: a stagger back, a fall onto the back, and the axe on the floor next to the hand.
issues: The haft passes near the hair at the top of the swing. The head test passes, but the margin is only 0.3 cm.
The tusks are small: about half the size of the mockup tusks. They hang down from under the upper lip, as the owner asked.
The beard is a small goatee, and the mockup beard is full.
next: Move the haft a little farther from the hair at the top of the swing, for a larger head margin.
Give the beard more volume, toward the full beard of the mockup.

bandit.summary: The bandit has its full clip set: idle, walk, run, a cutlass slash, hit, and death. The model matches the mockup: wild dark hair, an angry glare over a dark red mask, a striped shirt, a leather vest, a loot sack, and a curved cutlass. The death reads well. The slash is the weakest clip, because the wind-up is low and short.
strengths: The glare between the dark hair and the red mask is a strong focal point. It reads in the front view and in the S, SW, and SE sprites.
The death reads well. The bandit staggers, falls on its back, and lies flat with the face up. The cutlass drops from the hand and lies on the floor.
The slash has the three parts of a real cutlass cut: a wind-up, a cut with the edge leading, and a follow-through down and across the body. The sack and the mask tails swing late.
issues: The slash is a real cut, but a weak one. In the wind-up, the hand rises only to chest height, and the blade stays upright next to the shoulder. At the strike, the blade is level at waist height, so the cut reads as a flat sweep. The step into the cut is small.

The gear is plainer than the mockup. The mockup has straps on the vest, a holster at the belt, and tall boots with cuffs. The model has a plain vest and short boots. The sack still sits behind the arm.
The cutlass passes only 0.3 cm from the head in one clip (the check head margin). The check passes, but a small change to a clip can make it fail.
next: Make the slash stronger. Lift the hand above the shoulder and hold the blade back, then cut on a diagonal from high to the opposite hip. Make the forward step longer. Keep the head margin at 1 cm or more.
Add the mockup gear: a vest strap with a buckle, a holster at the belt, and cuffs on the boots. Move the sack a little to the side. These items from the last review are still open.

zombie.summary: The zombie now has the full clip set: idle, walk, run, attack, hit, and death. The silhouette, the colors, and the mismatched eyes match the mmx mockup. The hair, the shirt, and the trouser hems are still simpler than the mockup.
strengths: The bulging yellow eye and the glossy black eye read in every sprite direction that shows the face.
The death clip reads clearly. The head snaps back, the knees give way, and the body falls forward and lies flat. Nothing goes below the ground.
The walk and the run drag one foot and keep the arms forward, so the motion reads as a zombie at once.
issues: The hair is still a smooth black helmet with thick cone locks. The mockup hair is thinner and messier. In the back sprites, the hair is a large, plain black mass.

The shirt is still plain, with no torn collar, buttons, or loose threads. The trouser tears are still paint, and the sandals are flat planks. The collar and hem threads from the last review are still open.

The attack reads as a two-hand claw, and the forward pitch of the head and the chest gives it weight. But the reach is short: the hands rise only to the ears, the strike stops at belly height, and the feet stay planted.
next: Make the hair locks thinner and more varied, and break up the smooth mass at the back. This item from the last review is still open.
Add a lunge step to the attack, and extend the arms so that the claws reach past the face at chest height.

slime.summary: The slime is a glossy green jelly dome on a lobed puddle base, with three floating bubbles. The body and the face match the slime king mockup without the crown, the cape, and the chain. The jelly is opaque, so it shows less depth than the see-through mockup. All five clips read, but the slam does not travel far, and the death puddle shows the eyes at its rim.
strengths: The face reads at 128 px in the S sprite: big white eyes with lime irises, heavy brow ridges, and a frown.
The attack has clear squash and stretch: a low squash for anticipation, a tall stretch at the launch, a flat splat at the impact, and a rebound that settles.
The death melts the body into a wide puddle, and the bubbles swell and pop one after another. No clip goes below the ground (ground ok).
issues: The attack leap is almost vertical: the body moves 0.16 m forward and 0.2 m up. The slam reads as a hop in place, not a lunge at the target. At the end, the body slides back to the start without a hop.

In the death puddle, the eye whites stick out as white crescents at the rim, and the flat top shows radial shading streaks. The first 0.3 s shows almost no change, because the shudder is only 4 percent of the scale.
In the front view, a vertical ridge above the small frown reads as a nose. In the side view and the W and E sprites, the eye white sticks out of the profile as a white disc.
next: Make the slam a lunge: move the body about 0.35 m forward in an arc to the peak, and land on the target. Then hop back to the start in the recovery.
Fix the death puddle: hide the eyes inside the body before the puddle is flat, and remove the radial streaks on the top. Make the first 0.3 s a visible wobble or sag.

dire-wolf.summary: The dire wolf head matches the mmx mockup: cream brows, amber eyes, a toothy grin, cheek tufts, tall ears, and a cream ruff. A lower jaw on a jaw bone now opens, and the attack is a real leap and bite.
strengths: The lower jaw splits on the grin line. At rest the grin looks the same as before. Open, the mouth shows a dark inside, a pink tongue, and lower fangs.
The attack has a coiled crouch, a leap with the front paws off the ground and the jaw wide open, and a hard snap at the peak. The nose drives forward and down.
The ears, cheek tufts, and ruff make a spiky outline that reads in all 8 sprite directions at 128 px.
issues: The fur is one flat dark grey, and the cream muzzle is narrower than the wide grin in the mockup. The legs are straight, so the side view is longer than the compact mockup.
In the crouch the upper legs lean far forward, so the knees push out under the body. After the landing, the wolf hops back 20 cm to its start point, and the paws slide a little.
The hit and the death do not use the jaw. The yelp in the hit keeps the mouth shut.
next: Paint a lighter grey on the chest and the lower cheeks, and widen the cream muzzle toward the cheeks.
Open the jaw in the hit (a yelp) and a little in the death, so all clips use the new jaw.

giant-spider.summary: The giant spider is close to the mockup in the front view and reads clearly as a sprite. The attack now has a strong strike and a held bite. In the death, the body stays on the ground through the roll and lies on the small eyes and the abdomen. The eye colors are still open.
strengths: The front view is close to the mockup: the heavy brow, the glaring red eyes, the pale fangs, the orange splat, and the small eyeballs on top.
The attack reads: the spider rears up with the fangs wide, then pitches down 25 degrees and drives 16 cm forward in 0.08 s. The front feet slam down ahead, and the bite holds for 0.15 s.
In the death, the legs curl, the body drops onto its belly, rolls over the curled knees, and lies on its back. A measurement of every frame shows ground contact with no float.
issues: The big eyes still show a large red iris (cap 0.062 on an eye radius of 0.08) and a thin white ring.
The forward drive in the attack stops at 16 cm, not 20 cm. More drive pulls the back legs beyond their reach, and the back feet then slide.
In the attack strip, the fang snap is hard to see from the side, because the low head hides the fangs at the bite.
next: Fix the eye colors: a smaller red iris and a wider white ring, as in the mockup.
Check the fang snap in a front view of the attack. If it does not read, open the fangs wider at the top of the rear-up.

dragon-fire.summary: The fire dragon matches the mmx mockup closely in shape and color: a squat red dragon that is half head, with cream horns, a crest, heavy black brows, a toothy grin, orange bat wings, and a ridged cream belly. The attack is the weak clip: the strike points the open mouth at the floor, and no bite or breath reads.
strengths: The spread wings, the horns, and the crest make a unique silhouette that reads in all eight sprite directions.
The black brows over the yellow eyes and the white teeth in the dark grin give a strong focal point at 128 px.
The death has a clear stagger: the dragon rears with a last roar, then the legs buckle and it rolls onto its right side.
issues: The attack does not read as a bite or a breath. The windup tilts the head back only 16 degrees, and the chest does not fill. At the strike, the head pitches down about 30 degrees and the hips move only 4 cm forward, so the open mouth points at the floor and the strike looks like a nod. The recovery is present.
The head has no jaw bone, so the mouth keeps the same grin in every clip. The mockup puffs smoke from one nostril, and the model has no smoke or fire effect.
In the three-quarter view, the death ends with the head and the belly as two separate blobs, and the face lies sideways. The side view of the end pose reads clearly.
next: Rework the attack: scale the chest up about 8 percent in the windup, keep the head level at the strike, and move the hips 8 to 10 cm forward. Add a jaw bone that opens the mouth wide at the strike.
Add a fire-breath effect (an emissive cone from the mouth) that plays at the attack strike.

blacksmith.summary: The blacksmith matches the mmx mockup in costume and color: a red bandana, a black beard, a leather bib apron with brass rings, big gloves, and a hammer at the right shoulder. The body is less burly than the mockup, and the work blow is short. The check ends with result ok, but the head margin is only 0.3 cm.
strengths: The red bandana, the black beard, and the brown apron read at 128 px in all 8 sprite directions.
In the work clip, the drop is fast (about 0.12 s), and the hammer face is square to the work at the impact.
The talk clip shows a clear open-hand gesture in front of the chest, and the hammer stays still at the shoulder.
issues: The head is still larger than the torso. In the mockup, the chest and the arms are larger than the head, so the model is less burly than the mockup.

The work blow is not a full smith's blow. The fist rises only to chin height, and the side view hides the hammer behind the head during the lift. The blow lands out at the right side, not in front of the body. The rebound is only 2 cm, so it does not show.
The soot mark under the left eye is dark blue-gray and reads as a bruise in the front sprites. The back hair is one plain black mass.
next: Make the chest, the shoulders, and the arms 10 percent bigger. This item from the last review is still open.

In the work clip, raise the hammer head clearly above the bandana at the top of the lift, bring the blow in front of the belly, and make the rebound 5 to 6 cm. The higher lift from the last review is still open.

farmer.summary: The farmer model matches the mmx mockup well: a wide straw hat, a straw bundle in the mouth, a red plaid shirt, patched blue overalls, and a tall pitchfork. The work clip now reads as fork work: a stab into the soil, a lever, a lift of a hay clump, and a toss to his left. The short chibi arms limit the stab angle and the toss.
strengths: The wide straw hat and the tall pitchfork make a silhouette that reads as a farmer at once, also in the 128 px sprites.
The work clip uses targets: both hands hold the haft, the tines go 10 cm into the soil, and a hay clump rides from the lever to the toss.
The check passes: no held item goes through the head, and no clip sinks below the ground.
issues: The stab tilts the fork only 36 degrees down, not 55: the fork is 1 m long and the arms are 17 cm long, so a steeper fork hits the head.
The rig has no knees. The hips drop 5.6 cm because the pant legs squash, and the lean is small, so the crouch is weak in the three-quarter view.
At the toss the left fist moves up to 5 cm off the haft axis, and the haft touches the shirt, the overalls, and a brass button by up to 0.9 cm.
next: Add knee bones to the legs, so the stab can bend the knees and drop the hips more.
Make the fork shorter or move the top hand nearer the butt end, so the stab can tilt the fork more and keep both hands on the haft in the toss.

guard.summary: The town guard matches the mmx mockup in form. He has a kettle helmet with a crest, a brown mustache, and a blue tabard with a gold tower over mail. He has steel pauldrons, steel gauntlets, and a spear with a teal swallowtail pennant. The thrust now uses two hands in a side-on stance, with a draw back of about 10 cm. The face and the colors still differ from the mockup.
strengths: The kettle helmet with the crest, the gold tower on the tabard, the belt with the gold buckle, and the teal swallowtail pennant match the mockup.

The thrust reads in the strip. The guard turns side-on, the left hand holds the haft ahead of the right hand, the spear draws back about 10 cm, and then drives along the shaft with a step and a forward lean.
The clips are clean. The check gives result ok and ground ok, and no gauntlet goes into the body in the attack. In the run, the forearm lifts the spear, so the butt stays above the ground.
issues: The nose is small, and the mustache is flat and wide. The mockup has a large round nose and mustache tips that curl up. The steel is bright silver (#9aa0a8), not gunmetal, and the tabard is sky blue (#6aa2c0), not teal blue.
The chibi left arm is short. In the drive, the haft slides through the left hand, and the left shoulder moves forward up to 4.5 cm. The hand spacing changes from 0.20 to 0.36 m.
The right vambrace goes 0.4 cm into the tabard at phase 0.43 of the death. In the salute, the forearm stays inside the body outline.
next: Make the nose larger and rounder, and curl the mustache tips up. Darken the steel toward gunmetal (about #70767e), and move the tabard toward teal blue (about #4a93a6).
Move the right elbow out in the death at phase 0.43, so the vambrace clears the tabard.

skeleton-mage.summary: The skeleton mage matches the candle-skull caster on the mockup. The white wax now shows apart from the cream skull. The cast has an anticipation, a thrust toward the target, and a recovery. In the death, the mage staggers back, falls to the knees, drops the staff, and lies on its side. All clips pass the head check (margin 0.3 cm) and the ground check. The model has 43,126 triangles.
strengths: The candle on the skull is a unique silhouette. It shows clearly in all 8 sprite directions.
Three glowing accents (the candle flame, the palm flame, and the lantern) make the mage easy to see in a dark dungeon.
The death is clear: a stagger back, a fall to the knees, the staff falls to the floor, and the body lies on its side.
issues: The cast shows a real spell: the hand pulls back to the chest, then pushes the flame forward, then returns. But the palm flame keeps its size, and no bolt leaves the hand.
The known flaw is visible: after the death, the orange eyes stay lit on the skull on the floor. The candle flame also stays lit.
The candle is a wide block with a flat top, and the skull has no hood. The mockup has a taller, rounder candle and a dark hood. At 128 px, the wax drips cover part of the eye sockets.
next: At the release of the cast (phase 0.5), scale up the palm flame and make it brighter, or send a short purple bolt toward the target.
Put the eye glow on its own bone and scale it to zero at the end of the death. Scale the candle bone to zero there too.

imp.summary: The imp matches the imp on the Chibi Quest enemy sheet. It is a big-headed red devil with dark horns, amber eyes, fangs, bat wings, claws, and a spade tail. The wing bones are now dark brown. Three faults lower the score: flat light membranes, edge-on wing frames in the fly clip, and an attack that is only a head-first dive.
strengths: The spread bat wings and the curved horns give a spiky silhouette that reads in all eight sprite directions.
The dark brown wing bones now separate the wing frame from the membrane and repeat the horn color, as in the mockup.
The face reads at 128 px. The amber eyes under angry brows and the row of white fangs make it cute but dangerous.
issues: The attack has a small anticipation (the body leans back and the claws rise) and a smooth recovery. The strike is only a head-first dive. In the dive the arms swing back (upperarm +30), so the claws stay under the body and never reach toward the target. The wings keep the same beat through the dive.

The wings go edge-on in the fly clip. In the side view at t=0.13 to 0.19, both wings are one thin vertical line. In the three-quarter view at t=0.31 to 0.38, the near wing is almost invisible. The beat turns the wing only about Z, with no sweep or twist.

The membranes are one flat light orange (#e0704a), lighter than the skin, with sharp star points. The mockup membranes are darker red-orange with rounded scallops. The leading bone is dark and thick only to the knuckle; from the knuckle to the top tip it is a thin finger.
next: Make the attack a clear claw strike. Pull the claws back in the anticipation. Reach both claws forward at the target in the dive. Fold the wings back during the dive. Add a sweep and a twist to the wing beat so that no frame shows a wing edge-on.

Darken the membranes toward the wing tips with C.membraneDark. The file defines this color but does not use it. Carry the thick dark leading bone from the knuckle out to the top wing tip. Both requests from the old review are still open or only half done.

skeleton-archer.summary: The bow shot now draws to the jaw. The draw hand stops at the right side of the hood, at jaw height, above the mantle collar. The forearm lies level along the arrow line, and the elbow is high and back. The check passes (result ok, ground ok), and the draw, the hold, and the release have no body clips.
strengths: The draw hand comes to the right jaw (ANCHOR y = 0.46 m), and the forearm lies along the arrow line, level with the arrow.
The draw, the hold, and the release have no body clips: the wraps stay out of the ribs, and the hand and the bracer stay out of the mantle.
The shot keeps all its parts: the nock, the hold with a tremble, the string snap at the release, the follow-through past the jaw, and the recovery.
issues: In the front view, the bow arm crosses in front of the face and hides the draw hand. The mantle does not lift with the arm, so the upper arm and the high elbow go into the mantle and do not show.

In the reach to the quiver, the red wraps go 0.9 cm into the mantle at phase 0.04-0.08 and 0.23-0.30. Small old lines remain: the hand 0.4 cm into the cloak, the arrow 0.3 cm into the quiver, the string 0.4 cm into the cloak at phase 0.91.

The model differs from the mockup: the bow is a thin, upright stick, not a recurve across the body. The teeth are still one block with cut lines. At 128 px, the back and side sprites show only the hood and the quiver.
next: Give the skull separate teeth and make the bow a recurve, as the mockup shows.
Keep the red wraps out of the mantle hem in the reach to the quiver, and let the mantle show the raised draw arm.

giant-rat.summary: The giant rat matches the front of its mmx mockup: round pink-lined ears, red eyes under angry brows, a pink nose, buck teeth, head spikes, back tufts, a red neckerchief, and a ringed tail. The death reads well, but the attack does not read as a bite.
strengths: The round ears, the head spikes, the back tufts, and the long tail give a clear silhouette from every side and in all 8 sprite directions.
The red eyes under the angry brows, the pink nose, and the buck teeth on the cream muzzle read at 128 px in the front sprites.
The death has a recoil with the arms up, a fall onto the back, and one kick. Then the rat lies still with the paws up, above the ground.
issues: The attack does not read as a real rat bite. The rig has no jaw bone, so the jaws never open and never snap shut. The teeth stay in one fixed grin.
The wind-up leans the body back with the claws beside the head: a rear-up, not a crouch. In the lunge, the feet stay planted and the hips move only 6 cm, so there is no dart. The recovery is correct.

In the side view, the snout is still short and flat, and the body stands upright. The sides and the belly are smooth, with no fur clumps or folds. In the death, the rat stops in the rest pose for about 0.2 s before the fall.
next: Make the attack a real bite. Add a lower jaw on a jaw bone. Crouch low on bent legs, dart the hips about 15 cm forward with the jaws open, snap the jaws shut, then recover.

Push the snout and the nose 0.03 m forward, and lean the chest and the head forward. Add fur clumps along the sides and belly folds in the paint. The old review asked for these changes, and they are still open.

giant-bat.summary: The giant bat matches the front of its mmx mockup: a round purple fur ball, tall ears, yellow eyes under heavy brows, a pink snout, fangs, and pink wings on dark bones. The death reads well, but the attack does not read as a bite.
strengths: The front view and the S sprite read clearly at 128 px: the yellow eyes, the pink snout, the white fangs, and the wide pink wings.
The idle, the hit, and the death lift the ball into a hover. The wings beat on two bones each, so the wing tips lag the beat.
The death has a jolt in the hover, a tumble back, and a drop. Then the bat lies still on its back with the feet up. No clip sinks below the ground.
issues: The attack does not read as a real bat strike. The wings go up and the ball rises, but the rig has no jaw bone, so the mouth never opens and never snaps shut.
In the dive, the ball moves only 16 cm forward and drops 8 cm, and it pitches 32 degrees nose-down, so the face points at the floor. The climb back to the hover is correct.
The ears are still tall pointed triangles with a straight rim. In the side view and in the W and E sprites, the wings are still thin pink fins beside the ball.
next: Make the attack a real bite. Add a lower jaw on a jaw bone. Open the jaw wide in the dive, snap it shut at the target, and dive about 30 cm forward with a pitch of 15 degrees or less.
Round the ear outline and add two or three scallops to its back edge. Angle the wings 20 degrees toward the front at rest. The old review asked for these changes, and they are still open.

mimic.summary: The mimic matches its mmx mockup and uses the planks, iron, and gold lock of the treasure chest asset. The open lid is a jaw of white fangs with yellow slit eyes. Red flesh, a purple tongue, and iron claw feet complete it. Six clips cover the encounter: idle, walk, reveal, attack, hit, and death. The bite reads, and the death ends with the lid shut on the limp tongue.
strengths: Closed (the first frame of the reveal clip), the mimic matches the real treasure chest, so the trap works in a level.
The white teeth and the purple tongue read in every front and three-quarter sprite. The yellow eyes read best in the S sprite.
The death reads well. The chest shivers and gapes, the front legs buckle, then the back legs, and the lid falls shut on the limp tongue.
issues: The bite reads: the lid opens wide as the chest rears back, the chest lunges 14 cm forward, the lid slams shut, and the chest recovers. At the contact frame, the teeth shrink to half size and hide, so the bite shows a plain closed chest.
The mockup shows gold coins and cloth in the flesh; the model has only flesh. The teeth are still straight cones with thin bases.
The chest body is a square box; the mockup chest flares out toward the top. The iron bands are blue-black; the mockup iron is a warm dark gray-brown.
next: Add a few gold coins and a gem in the flesh, from the treasure heap of the chest. This item from the old review is still open.
Make the tooth bases thicker and bend the middle teeth a little toward the front. Keep the tooth tips visible at the seam when the lid slams shut. The tooth item from the old review is still open.

animated-armor.summary: The animated armor matches its mmx mockup: a huge round great helm with a brass band, a black visor with two cyan eyes, and a slotted face plate. The dark suit has rust specks, a purple scarf, a torn cape, and a broad sword. This pass changed three clips and not the model. In the run, the fist comes up to the belt and the blade points flatter across the front, so the tip stays about 8 cm above the floor. In the attack, the follow-through keeps the right forearm clear of the cuirass. In the death, the cape falls off the collar and lies flat on the floor behind the pile. ./forge check gives result ok and ground ok.
strengths: The two cyan eyes on the black visor read at once, also in the 128 px sprites. Nothing inside the helm shows that the suit is empty.

The slash reads as a real sword cut. The blade rises up and back beside the helm and holds, then cuts across the front with the edge first. The follow-through ends low at the left, and the right forearm stays about 1 cm clear of the cuirass.
The death tells the story: the eyes flicker out, the sword drops flat, the helm falls off in front and rolls onto its side, the legs splay, and the cape lies flat on the floor behind the pile.
issues: The helm is a smooth round dome. The mockup helm has a raised brow over the visor and cheek plates that flare out.
The rust specks on the helm dome and the pauldrons are still small and sparse. The suit looks cleaner than the mockup.

In the attack, the top of the backswing is behind the helm in the front view, so the front sprite shows mainly the follow-through. The run carries the blade in a flat guard, which is less menacing than the low carry in the walk.
next: Give the helm a raised brow ridge over the visor, and flare the cheek plates out as in the mockup.
Add more rust patches and scratches on the helm dome and the pauldrons.
